7removed-- # Imp: Simple Imperative Programs
8removed
9removed-- Note to developers (before next release):
10removed-- Needs some WORKINCLASSes and some quizzes
11removed--
12removed-- LATER: Another nice challenge exercise at some point
13removed-- would be to add C-style arrays (i.e., indirect
14removed-- read/write). This sets up some really nice challenge
15removed-- problems in Hoare (reasoning about arrays / aliasing /
16removed-- etc.).
17removed--
18removed-- SOONER: BCP 25: Maybe we should write / instead of && in
19removed-- assertions, to save a mismatch in the `dec_minimum`
20removed-- exercise in Hoare2?
21removed--
22removed-- At some point we could consider moving material from the
23removed-- old HoareLists to this chapter (and into later files, as
24removed-- appropriate). We haven't done it yet because it's a
25removed-- shame to complicate the nice simple presentation here
26removed-- when it's used as the basis for applications like
27removed-- Xavier's static analysis lectures. Also, we now have a
28removed-- whole volume on real separation logic...
29removed--
30removed-- MWH (port note): The Rocq chapter's "Rocq Automation"
31removed-- tour has been retooled here for Lean. The tactic
32removed-- combinators `try` and `repeat` (and the custom-tactic
33removed-- `macro`) are introduced in this chapter; `<;>` and
34removed-- `simp` were already introduced in Logical Foundations
35removed-- (`<;>` in `Induction`) so we use them freely and the
36removed-- `<;>` section below is a recap. For linear arithmetic we
37removed-- use `lia`; NOTE that LF currently introduces `omega`,
38removed-- not `lia`, so this needs to be reconciled volume-wide
39removed-- (either introduce `lia` in LF, or keep `omega`).
40removed
41removed-- We concentrate here on defining the *syntax* and *semantics*
42removed-- of Imp; later in this volume we develop a theory of *program
43removed-- equivalence* and introduce *Hoare Logic*, a popular logic
44removed-- for reasoning about imperative programs.
45removed
46removed-- ## Expressions With Variables
47removed
48removed-- ### States
49removed
50removed-- Since we'll want to look variables up to find out their
51removed-- current values, we'll use total maps from the `Maps`
52removed-- chapter. A *machine state* (or just *state*) represents the
53removed-- current values of all variables at some point in the
54removed-- execution of a program.
55removed
56removed-- We give the type of variable identifiers a name, `Ident`.
57removed-- For now it is just `String`; naming it makes the intent
58removed-- clearer.
59removed
60removedabbrev Ident := String
61removedabbrev State := TotalMap Ident Nat
62removed
63removed-- ### Syntax
64removed
65removed-- We can add variables to the arithmetic expressions we had
66removed-- before simply by including one more constructor. (This is a
67removed-- fresh `Aexp`, replacing the variable-free one from the
68removed-- *Slang* chapter.)
69removed
70removed-- Note to developers (Benjamin Pierce @bcpierce00):
71removed-- That should be a live chapter link.
72removed
73removedinductive Aexp where
74removed | num (n : Nat)
75removed | id (x : Ident) -- NEW
76removed | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
77removed | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
78removed | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp)
79removed
80removed-- Note to developers (Chris Henson @chenson2018):
81removed-- Rather than define identifiers as Ident, a more general
82removed-- approach is to use a **type variable** with
83removed-- `DecidableEq` (as the `Maps` chapter does), threaded
84removed-- through `Aexp`/`Bexp`/`Com`/`State`. Stashed for a
85removed-- future decision; the parameterized version would look
86removed-- like:
87removed--
88removed-- `inductive Aexp (V : Type) where
89removed-- | num (n : Nat)
90removed-- | id (x : V)
91removed-- | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp V)
92removed-- | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp V)
93removed-- | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp V)
94removed-- -- … then `Bexp V`, `Com V`, `abbrev State (V) [DecidableEq V] :=
95removed-- -- TotalMap V Nat`, and `[DecidableEq V]` wherever a lookup/update is
96removed-- -- performed.`
97removed
98removed-- The `Bexp` definition is unchanged, except that it now
99removed-- refers to the new `Aexp`.
100removed
101removedinductive Bexp where
102removed | bool (b : Bool)
103removed | eq (a1 a2 : Aexp)
104removed | neq (a1 a2 : Aexp)
105removed | le (a1 a2 : Aexp)
106removed | gt (a1 a2 : Aexp)
107removed | not (b : Bexp)
108removed | and (b1 b2 : Bexp)
109removed
110removed-- Defining a few variable names as shorthands will make
111removed-- examples easier to read.
112removed
113removeddef W : Ident := "W"
114removeddef X : Ident := "X"
115removeddef Y : Ident := "Y"
116removeddef Z : Ident := "Z"
117removed

119removed
120removed/-- Arithmetic expressions of Imp -/
121removeddeclare_syntax_cat imp_aexp
122removed/-- Numeric literal -/
123removedsyntax:max num : imp_aexp
124removed/-- Variable reference -/
125removedsyntax:max ident : imp_aexp
126removed/-- Addition -/
127removedsyntax:65 imp_aexp:65 " + " imp_aexp:66 : imp_aexp
128removed/-- Subtraction -/
129removedsyntax:65 imp_aexp:65 " - " imp_aexp:66 : imp_aexp
130removed/-- Multiplication -/
131removedsyntax:70 imp_aexp:70 " * " imp_aexp:71 : imp_aexp
132removed/-- Parentheses for grouping -/

134removed/-- Escape to Lean -/
135removedsyntax:max "~" term:max : imp_aexp
136removed

140removedopen Lean in
141removedmacro_rules
142removed | `(aexp { $n:num }) => `(Aexp.num $(quote n.getNat))
143removed | `(aexp { $x:ident }) => `(Aexp.id $x)
144removed | `(aexp { ~$e }) => pure e
145removed | `(aexp { $a + $b }) => `(Aexp.plus (aexp {$a}) (aexp {$b}))
146removed | `(aexp { $a - $b }) => `(Aexp.minus (aexp {$a}) (aexp {$b}))
147removed | `(aexp { $a * $b }) => `(Aexp.mult (aexp {$a}) (aexp {$b}))
148removed | `(aexp { ($a) }) => `(aexp {$a})

151removed
152removed/-- Boolean expressions of Imp -/
153removeddeclare_syntax_cat imp_bexp
154removed/-- Boolean literal (`true` or `false`) -/
155removedsyntax:max ident : imp_bexp
156removed/-- Equality of arithmetic expressions -/
157removedsyntax:50 imp_aexp:51 " = " imp_aexp:51 : imp_bexp
158removed/-- Disequality of arithmetic expressions -/

162removed/-- Greater than -/

164removed/-- Boolean negation -/
165removedsyntax:70 "¬ " imp_bexp:70 : imp_bexp
166removed/-- Boolean conjunction -/

168removed/-- Parentheses for grouping -/
169removedsyntax "(" imp_bexp ")" : imp_bexp
170removed/-- Escape to Lean -/
171removedsyntax:max "~" term:max : imp_bexp
172removed
173removed/-- Embed an Imp boolean expression into a Lean term -/
174removedsyntax:min "bexp " "{" imp_bexp "}" : term
175removed
176removed-- _Details:_ Notation encoding: boolean expressions, macro rules
177removed
178removedopen Lean in
179removedmacro_rules
180removed | `(bexp { $x:ident }) =>
181removed match x.getId with
182removed | `true => `(Bexp.bool true)
183removed | `false => `(Bexp.bool false)
184removed | _ => Macro.throwErrorAt x s!"expected 'true' or 'false', got '{x.getId}'"
185removed | `(bexp { ~$e }) => pure e
186removed | `(bexp { $a:imp_aexp = $b:imp_aexp }) => `(Bexp.eq (aexp {$a}) (aexp {$b}))
187removed | `(bexp { $a:imp_aexp ≠ $b:imp_aexp }) => `(Bexp.neq (aexp {$a}) (aexp {$b}))
188removed | `(bexp { $a:imp_aexp ≤ $b:imp_aexp }) => `(Bexp.le (aexp {$a}) (aexp {$b}))
189removed | `(bexp { $a:imp_aexp > $b:imp_aexp }) => `(Bexp.gt (aexp {$a}) (aexp {$b}))
190removed | `(bexp { ¬ $b:imp_bexp }) => `(Bexp.not (bexp {$b}))
191removed | `(bexp { $b1:imp_bexp ∧ $b2:imp_bexp }) => `(Bexp.and (bexp {$b1}) (bexp {$b2}))
192removed | `(bexp { ($b:imp_bexp) }) => `(bexp {$b})
193removed
194removedinstance : Coe Ident Aexp where
195removed coe := .id
196removed
197removedinstance (n : Nat) : OfNat Aexp n where
198removed ofNat := .num n
199removed
200removedinstance : Coe Bool Bexp where
201removed coe := .bool
202removed
203removeddef example_aexp : Aexp := aexp { 3 + (X * 2) }
204removeddef example_bexp : Bexp := bexp { true ∧ ¬(X ≤ 4) }

206removed-- ### Delaborators
207removed
208removed-- _Details:_ Notation encoding: printing expressions back
209removed
210removednamespace Imp.Delab
211removedopen Lean PrettyPrinter Delaborator SubExpr Parenthesizer
212removed
213removed/-- Re-inserts parentheses in `imp_aexp` output according to the grammar's precedences. -/
214removed@[category_parenthesizer imp_aexp]
215removeddef imp_aexp.parenthesizer : CategoryParenthesizer | prec => do
216removed maybeParenthesize `imp_aexp true wrapParens prec <|
217removed parenthesizeCategoryCore `imp_aexp prec
218removedwhere
219removed wrapParens (stx : Syntax) : Syntax := Unhygienic.run do
220removed let pstx ← `(($(⟨stx⟩)))
221removed return pstx.raw.setInfo (SourceInfo.fromRef stx)
222removed
223removed/-- Re-inserts parentheses in `imp_bexp` output according to the grammar's precedences. -/
224removed@[category_parenthesizer imp_bexp]
225removeddef imp_bexp.parenthesizer : CategoryParenthesizer | prec => do
226removed maybeParenthesize `imp_bexp true wrapParens prec <|
227removed parenthesizeCategoryCore `imp_bexp prec
228removedwhere
229removed wrapParens (stx : Syntax) : Syntax := Unhygienic.run do
230removed let pstx ← `(($(⟨stx⟩)))
231removed return pstx.raw.setInfo (SourceInfo.fromRef stx)
232removed
233removed/-- Tag freshly built syntax with the term info that Lean's pretty printer expects. -/
234removeddef annAsTerm {any} (stx : TSyntax any) : DelabM (TSyntax any) :=
235removed (⟨·⟩) <$> annotateTermInfo ⟨stx.raw⟩
236removed
237removed/-- Rebuild `imp_aexp` concrete syntax from an `Aexp` term. -/
238removedpartial def delabAexpInner : DelabM (TSyntax `imp_aexp) := do
239removed let e ← getExpr
240removed let stx ←
241removed match_expr e with
242removed | Aexp.num _ =>
243removed match (← withAppArg getExpr).nat? with
244removed | some v => pure ⟨Syntax.mkNumLit (toString v) |>.raw⟩
245removed | none => `(imp_aexp| ~$(← withAppArg delab))
246removed | Aexp.id _ =>
247removed -- A variable reference like aexp { X } elaborates to Aexp.id X where X is the
248removed -- declared Ident constant, so the delaborators print the constant's name as a
249removed -- bare identifier (and also handle the .id "X" string-literal form).
250removed match ← withAppArg getExpr with
251removed | .const nm _ => `(imp_aexp| $(mkIdent nm):ident)
252removed | .lit (.strVal s) => `(imp_aexp| $(mkIdent (.mkSimple s)):ident)
253removed | _ => `(imp_aexp| ~$(← withAppArg delab))
254removed | Aexp.plus _ _ =>
255removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabAexpInner
256removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabAexpInner
257removed `(imp_aexp| $s1 + $s2)
258removed | Aexp.minus _ _ =>
259removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabAexpInner
260removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabAexpInner
261removed `(imp_aexp| $s1 - $s2)
262removed | Aexp.mult _ _ =>
263removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabAexpInner
264removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabAexpInner
265removed `(imp_aexp| $s1 * $s2)
266removed | _ => `(imp_aexp| ~$(← delab))
267removed annAsTerm stx
268removed
269removed/-- Rebuild `imp_bexp` concrete syntax from a `Bexp` term. -/
270removedpartial def delabBexpInner : DelabM (TSyntax `imp_bexp) := do
271removed let e ← getExpr
272removed let stx ←
273removed match_expr e with
274removed | Bexp.bool _ =>
275removed match ← withAppArg getExpr with
276removed | .const ``Bool.true _ => `(imp_bexp| $(mkIdent `true):ident)
277removed | .const ``Bool.false _ => `(imp_bexp| $(mkIdent `false):ident)
278removed | _ => `(imp_bexp| ~$(← withAppArg delab))
279removed | Bexp.eq _ _ =>
280removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabAexpInner
281removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabAexpInner
282removed `(imp_bexp| $s1:imp_aexp = $s2:imp_aexp)
283removed | Bexp.neq _ _ =>
284removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabAexpInner
285removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabAexpInner
286removed `(imp_bexp| $s1:imp_aexp ≠ $s2:imp_aexp)
287removed | Bexp.le _ _ =>
288removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabAexpInner
289removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabAexpInner
290removed `(imp_bexp| $s1:imp_aexp ≤ $s2:imp_aexp)
291removed | Bexp.gt _ _ =>
292removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabAexpInner
293removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabAexpInner
294removed `(imp_bexp| $s1:imp_aexp > $s2:imp_aexp)
295removed | Bexp.not _ =>
296removed let s ← withAppArg delabBexpInner
297removed `(imp_bexp| ¬ $s)
298removed | Bexp.and _ _ =>
299removed let s1 ← withAppFn <| withAppArg delabBexpInner
300removed let s2 ← withAppArg delabBexpInner
301removed `(imp_bexp| $s1 ∧ $s2)
302removed | _ => `(imp_bexp| ~$(← delab))
303removed annAsTerm stx
304removed
305removed-- The `whenPPOption getPPNotation` wrapper lets
306removed-- `set_option pp.notation false` switch this delaborator off,
307removed-- revealing the raw constructors (see the "Desugaring
308removed-- Notations" discussion, after the commands are introduced).
309removed
310removed-- _Details:_ Notation encoding: registering the delaborators
311removed
312removed@[delab app.Aexp.num, delab app.Aexp.id, delab app.Aexp.plus,
313removed delab app.Aexp.minus, delab app.Aexp.mult]
314removedpartial def delabAexp : Delab := whenPPOption getPPNotation do
315removed -- This delaborator only understands `Aexp`'s constructors -- bail otherwise.
316removed guard <| match_expr ← getExpr with
317removed | Aexp.num _ => true
318removed | Aexp.id _ => true
319removed | Aexp.plus _ _ => true
320removed | Aexp.minus _ _ => true
321removed | Aexp.mult _ _ => true
322removed | _ => false
323removed match ← delabAexpInner with
324removed | `(imp_aexp| ~$e) => pure e
325removed | e => `(term| aexp { $e })
326removed
327removed@[delab app.Bexp.bool, delab app.Bexp.eq, delab app.Bexp.neq, delab app.Bexp.le,
328removed delab app.Bexp.gt, delab app.Bexp.not, delab app.Bexp.and]
329removedpartial def delabBexp : Delab := whenPPOption getPPNotation do
330removed guard <| match_expr ← getExpr with
331removed | Bexp.bool _ => true
332removed | Bexp.eq _ _ => true
333removed | Bexp.neq _ _ => true
334removed | Bexp.le _ _ => true
335removed | Bexp.gt _ _ => true
336removed | Bexp.not _ => true
337removed | Bexp.and _ _ => true
338removed | _ => false
339removed match ← delabBexpInner with
340removed | `(imp_bexp| ~$e) => pure e
341removed | e => `(term| bexp { $e })
342removed
343removedend Imp.Delab

345removed#check aexp { 3 + (X * 2) }
346removed
347removed#check bexp { true ∧ ¬(X ≤ 4) }

349removed-- ### Evaluation
350removed
351removed-- Now we need to add an `st` parameter to both evaluation
352removed-- functions:
353removed
354removedopen scoped MyGetElem
355removed
356removeddef Aexp.eval (st : State) (a : Aexp) : Nat :=
357removed match a with
358removed | num n => n
359removed | id x => st[x] -- NEW
360removed | plus a1 a2 => a1.eval st + a2.eval st
361removed | minus a1 a2 => a1.eval st - a2.eval st
362removed | mult a1 a2 => a1.eval st * a2.eval st
363removed
364removeddef Bexp.eval (st : State) (b : Bexp) : Bool :=
365removed match b with
366removed | bool b => b
367removed | eq a1 a2 => a1.eval st == a2.eval st
368removed | neq a1 a2 => a1.eval st != a2.eval st
369removed | le a1 a2 => a1.eval st ≤ a2.eval st
370removed | gt a1 a2 => a1.eval st > a2.eval st
371removed | not b1 => !b1.eval st
372removed | and b1 b2 => b1.eval st && b2.eval st
373removed
374removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_num (st : State) (n : Nat) : (num n).eval st = n := rfl
375removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_id (st : State) (x : Ident) : (Aexp.id x).eval st = st[x] := rfl
376removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_plus (st : State) (a1 a2 : Aexp) :
377removed (plus a1 a2).eval st = a1.eval st + a2.eval st := rfl
378removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_minus (st : State) (a1 a2 : Aexp) :
379removed (minus a1 a2).eval st = a1.eval st - a2.eval st := rfl
380removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_mult (st : State) (a1 a2 : Aexp) :
381removed (mult a1 a2).eval st = a1.eval st * a2.eval st := rfl
382removed
383removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_bool (st : State) (b : Bool) : (bool b).eval st = b := rfl
384removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_eq (st : State) (a1 a2 : Aexp) :
385removed (eq a1 a2).eval st = (a1.eval st == a2.eval st) := rfl
386removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_neq (st : State) (a1 a2 : Aexp) :
387removed (neq a1 a2).eval st = (a1.eval st != a2.eval st) := rfl
388removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_le (st : State) (a1 a2 : Aexp) :
389removed (le a1 a2).eval st = (a1.eval st ≤ a2.eval st : Bool) := rfl
390removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_gt (st : State) (a1 a2 : Aexp) :
391removed (gt a1 a2).eval st = (a1.eval st > a2.eval st : Bool) := rfl
392removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_not (st : State) (b : Bexp) : (not b).eval st = !b.eval st := rfl
393removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_and (st : State) (b1 b2 : Bexp) :
394removed (and b1 b2).eval st = (b1.eval st && b2.eval st) := rfl
395removed
396removed-- We reuse the total-map notation (`x →ₜ v ; ∅` etc.) for
397removed-- states.
398removed
399removedexample : aexp { 3 + (X * 2) }.eval (X →ₜ 5 ; ∅) = 13 := by rfl
400removed
401removedexample : aexp { Z + (X * Y) }.eval (X →ₜ 5 ; Y →ₜ 4 ; ∅) = 20 := by rfl
402removed
403removedexample : bexp { true ∧ ¬(X ≤ 4) }.eval (X →ₜ 5 ; ∅) = true := by rfl
404removed

406removed-- dsainati: Bikeshedding: I'm not sure how I feel about

412removed-- ## Commands
413removed
414removedinductive Com where
415removed | skip
416removed | asgn (x : Ident) (a : Aexp)
417removed | seq (c1 c2 : Com)
418removed | cond (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com)
419removed | whileDo (b : Bexp) (c : Com)
420removed
421removed-- _Details:_ Notation encoding: commands
422removed
423removed/-- Imp commands -/
424removeddeclare_syntax_cat imp_com
425removed
426removed-- _Details:_ Notation encoding: commands, macro rules
427removed
428removed/-- The command that does nothing (`skip;`) -/
429removedsyntax ident ";" : imp_com
430removed/-- Sequencing: one command after another -/
431removedsyntax imp_com ppDedent(ppLine imp_com) : imp_com
432removed/-- Assignment -/
433removedsyntax ident " := " imp_aexp ";" : imp_com
434removed/-- Conditional -/
435removedsyntax "if " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine imp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}" ppHardSpace "else" ppHardSpace "{") ppLine imp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : imp_com
436removed/-- Loop -/
437removedsyntax "while " "(" imp_bexp ")" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine imp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : imp_com
438removed/-- Escape to Lean -/
439removedsyntax:max "~" term:max : imp_com
440removed
441removed/-- Include an Imp command in Lean code -/
442removedsyntax:min "imp" ppHardSpace "{" ppLine imp_com ppDedent(ppLine "}") : term
443removed
444removedopen Lean in
445removedmacro_rules
446removed | `(imp { $x:ident ; }) =>
447removed if x.getId == `skip then `(Com.skip)
448removed else Macro.throwErrorAt x s!"expected 'skip', got '{x.getId}'"
449removed | `(imp { $c1 $c2 }) =>
450removed `(Com.seq (imp {$c1}) (imp {$c2}))
451removed | `(imp { $x:ident := $a; }) =>
452removed `(Com.asgn $x (aexp {$a}))
453removed | `(imp { if ($b) {$c1} else {$c2} }) =>
454removed `(Com.cond (bexp {$b}) (imp {$c1}) (imp {$c2}))
455removed | `(imp { while ($b) {$c} }) =>
456removed `(Com.whileDo (bexp {$b}) (imp {$c}))
457removed | `(imp { ~$c }) =>
458removed pure c
459removed
460removed-- _Details:_ Notation encoding: printing commands back
461removed
462removednamespace Imp.Delab
463removedopen Lean PrettyPrinter Delaborator SubExpr
464removed
465removed/-- Rebuild `imp_com` concrete syntax from a `Com` term. -/
466removedpartial def delabComInner : DelabM (TSyntax `imp_com) := do
467removed let e ← getExpr
468removed let stx ←
469removed match_expr e with
470removed | Com.skip => `(imp_com| skip;)
471removed | Com.asgn _ _ =>
472removed match ← withAppFn <| withAppArg getExpr with
473removed | .const nm _ =>

574removed-- ## Evaluating Commands
575removed
576removed-- ### Evaluation as a Function (Failed Attempt)
577removed
578removed-- Here's an attempt at defining an evaluation function for
579removed-- commands (with a bogus `while` case).
580removed
581removeddef Com.ceval_fun_no_while (st : State) (c : Com) : State :=
582removed match c with
583removed | imp {skip;} => st
584removed | imp {x := ~a;} => (x →ₜ a.eval st ; st)
585removed | imp {~c1 ~c2} =>
586removed let st' := ceval_fun_no_while st c1
587removed ceval_fun_no_while st' c2
588removed | imp {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2}} =>
589removed if b.eval st then ceval_fun_no_while st c1
590removed else ceval_fun_no_while st c2
591removed | imp {while (~_) {~_}} => st -- bogus
592removed
593removed-- Note to developers:
594removed-- Perhaps that discussion should be moved to -- or
595removed-- previewed in -- Logic.v? MRC'20: It's already in
596removed-- ProofObjects (which not everyone sees).
597removed
598removed-- A nonterminating
599removed-- `def loop_false (n) : False := loop_false n` would make
600removed-- `False` provable, so Lean rejects it.
601removed
602removed-- ### Evaluation as a Relation
603removed
604removed-- Here's a better way: define `ceval` as a *relation* rather
605removed-- than a *function* -- i.e., make its result a `Prop` rather
606removed-- than a `State`, similar to what we did for `Aexp.EvalR`
607removed-- above.
608removed
609removed-- Note to developers (Michael Hicks @mwhicks1):
610removed-- I kind of hate this notation. Is there something more
611removed-- standard in Lean? CSLib precedent maybe?
612removed
613removed-- We'll use the notation `st =[ c ]=> st'` for the `Com.EvalR`
614removed-- relation: `st =[ c ]=> st'` means that executing program `c`
615removed-- in a starting state `st` results in an ending state `st'`.
616removed-- This can be pronounced "`c` takes state `st` to `st'`".
617removed
618removed-- Operational Semantics
619removed
620removed-- Note to developers (before next release):
621removed-- BCP 21: I wonder if `seq` would be easier to work with
622removed-- if st' and st'' were swapped...
623removed
624removed-- Here is an informal definition of evaluation, presented as
625removed-- inference rules for readability:
626removed
627removed-- ----------------- (skip)
628removed-- st =[ skip ]=> st
629removed
630removed-- a.eval st = n
631removed-- -------------------------------- (asgn)
632removed-- st =[ x := a ]=> (x →ₜ n ; st)
633removed
634removed-- st =[ c1 ]=> st'
635removed-- st' =[ c2 ]=> st''
636removed-- --------------------- (seq)
637removed-- st =[ c1;c2 ]=> st''
638removed
639removed-- b.eval st = true
640removed-- st =[ c1 ]=> st'
641removed-- -------------------------------------- (ifTrue)
642removed-- st =[ if b then c1 else c2 end ]=> st'
643removed
644removed-- b.eval st = false
645removed-- st =[ c2 ]=> st'
646removed-- -------------------------------------- (ifFalse)
647removed-- st =[ if b then c1 else c2 end ]=> st'
648removed
649removed-- b.eval st = false
650removed-- ----------------------------- (whileFalse)
651removed-- st =[ while b do c end ]=> st
652removed
653removed-- b.eval st = true
654removed-- st =[ c ]=> st'
655removed-- st' =[ while b do c end ]=> st''
656removed-- -------------------------------- (whileTrue)
657removed-- st =[ while b do c end ]=> st''
658removed
659removed-- Here is the formal definition. Make sure you understand how
660removed-- it corresponds to the inference rules.
661removed
662removed-- Note to developers (Chris Henson @chenson2018):
663removed-- TODO Propose you use inline notation such as
664removed-- `Com.EvalR (imp {skip;}) st st`
665removed
666removedinductive Com.EvalR : Com → State → State → Prop where
667removed | skip (st : State) : EvalR (imp {skip;}) st st
668removed | asgn (st : State) (a : Aexp) (n : Nat) (x : Ident) (h : a.eval st = n) :
669removed EvalR (imp {x := ~a;}) st (x →ₜ n ; st)
670removed | seq (c1 c2 : Com) (st st' st'' : State) (h1 : EvalR c1 st st') (h2 : EvalR c2 st' st'') :
671removed EvalR (imp {~c1 ~c2}) st st''
672removed | ifTrue (st st' : State) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com) (hb : b.eval st = true)
673removed (hc : EvalR c1 st st') :
674removed EvalR (imp {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2}}) st st'
675removed | ifFalse (st st' : State) (b : Bexp) (c1 c2 : Com) (hb : b.eval st = false)
676removed (hc : EvalR c2 st st') :
677removed EvalR (imp {if (~b) {~c1} else {~c2}}) st st'
678removed | whileFalse (b : Bexp) (st : State) (c : Com) (hb : b.eval st = false) :
679removed EvalR (imp {while (~b) {~c}}) st st
680removed | whileTrue (st st' st'' : State) (b : Bexp) (c : Com) (hb : b.eval st = true)
681removed (hc : EvalR c st st') (hloop : Com.EvalR (imp {while (~b) {~c}}) st' st'') :
682removed EvalR (imp {while (~b) {~c}}) st st''
683removed
684removednotation:40 st0:41 " =[ " c " ]=> " st1:41 => Com.EvalR c st0 st1
685removed-- Also accept a bare Imp command between the brackets, so concrete programs can
686removed-- be written without the `imp { … }` wrapper. Bare `Com` terms still work via the
687removed-- notation above; splice a Lean term into the command with `~`.
688removedsyntax:40 term:41 " =[ " imp_com " ]=> " term:41 : term
689removedmacro_rules
690removed | `($st0 =[ $c:imp_com ]=> $st1) => `($st0 =[ imp { $c } ]=> $st1)
691removed
692removed-- The cost of defining evaluation as a relation instead of a
693removed-- function is that we now need to construct a *proof* that
694removed-- some program evaluates to some result state, rather than
695removed-- letting Lean's computation mechanism do it for us.
696removed
697removedexample :
698removed ∅ =[
699removed X := 2;
700removed if (X ≤ 1) {
701removed Y := 3;
702removed } else {
703removed Z := 4;
704removed }
705removed ]=> (Z →ₜ 4 ; X →ₜ 2 ; ∅) := by
706removed -- We must supply the intermediate state.
707removed apply Com.EvalR.seq (st' := (X →ₜ 2 ; ∅))
708removed · apply Com.EvalR.asgn; rfl
709removed · apply Com.EvalR.ifFalse
710removed · rfl
711removed · apply Com.EvalR.asgn; rfl
712removed
713removed-- ### Exercise (2 stars): ceval_example2 ⭐⭐
714removed
715removedexample :
716removed ∅ =[
717removed X := 0;
718removed Y := 1;
719removed Z := 2;
720removed ]=> (Z →ₜ 2 ; Y →ₜ 1 ; X →ₜ 0 ; ∅) := by
721removed sorry
722removed
723removed-- What sorts of things might we want to prove using these
724removed-- definitions? Here are some simple examples...
725removed
726removed-- Note to developers:
727removed-- PR: I phrased these quizzes with the following
728removed-- alternatives: (A) Not true (B) True and easily provable
729removed-- (C) True and takes more work to prove (D) True and
730removed-- cannot be proved without additional axioms
731removed
732removed-- _Quiz:_
733removed
734removed-- Is the following proposition provable?
735removed
736removed-- ∀ (c : Com) (st st' : State),
737removed-- st =[ skip; ~c ]=> st' →
738removed-- st =[ c ]=> st'
739removed
740removed-- (A) Yes (B) No (C) Not sure
741removed
742removed-- _Quiz:_
743removed
744removed-- Is the following proposition provable?
745removed
746removed-- ∀ (c1 c2 : Com) (st st' : State),
747removed-- st =[ ~c1 ~c2 ]=> st' →
748removed-- st =[ c1 ]=> st →
749removed-- st =[ c2 ]=> st'
750removed
751removed-- (A) Yes (B) No (C) Not sure
752removed
753removed-- _Quiz:_
754removed
755removed-- Is the following proposition provable?
756removed
757removed-- ∀ (b : Bexp) (c : Com) (st st' : State),
758removed-- st =[ if (~b) { ~c } else { ~c } ]=> st' →
759removed-- st =[ c ]=> st'
760removed
761removed-- (A) Yes (B) No (C) Not sure
762removed
763removed-- _Quiz:_
764removed
765removed-- Is the following proposition provable?
766removed
767removed-- ∀ (b : Bexp),
768removed-- (∀ st, b.eval st = true) →
769removed-- ∀ (c : Com) (st : State),
770removed-- ¬ ∃ st', st =[ while (~b) { ~c } ]=> st'
771removed
772removed-- (A) Yes (B) No (C) Not sure
773removed
774removed-- _Quiz:_
775removed
776removed-- Is the following proposition provable?
777removed
778removed-- ∀ (b : Bexp) (c : Com) (st : State),
779removed-- (¬ ∃ st', st =[ while (~b) { ~c } ]=> st') →
780removed-- ∀ st'', b.eval st'' = true
781removed
782removed-- (A) Yes (B) No (C) Not sure
783removed
784removed-- ### Determinism of Evaluation
785removed
786removed-- Finally, we should pause to check that our evaluation
787removed-- relation really is a (partial) function...
788removed
789removedtheorem ceval_deterministic (c : Com) (st st1 st2 : State)
790removed (e1 : st =[ c ]=> st1) (e2 : st =[ c ]=> st2) : st1 = st2 := by
791removed induction e1 generalizing st2 with
792removed | skip st =>
793removed cases e2 with
794removed | skip => rfl
795removed | asgn st a n x h =>
796removed cases e2 with
797removed | asgn _ _ n' _ h' => subst h; subst h'; rfl
798removed | seq c1 c2 st st' st'' h1 h2 ih1 ih2 =>
799removed cases e2 with
800removed | seq _ _ _ st2' _ h1' h2' =>
801removed have hst : st' = st2' := ih1 _ h1'
802removed subst hst
803removed exact ih2 _ h2'
804removed | ifTrue st st' b c1 c2 hb hc ih =>
805removed cases e2 with
806removed | ifTrue _ _ _ _ _ hb' hc' => exact ih _ hc'
807removed | ifFalse _ _ _ _ _ hb' hc' => simp_all
808removed | ifFalse st st' b c1 c2 hb hc ih =>
809removed cases e2 with
810removed | ifTrue _ _ _ _ _ hb' hc' => simp_all
811removed | ifFalse _ _ _ _ _ hb' hc' => exact ih _ hc'
812removed | whileFalse b st c hb =>
813removed cases e2 with
814removed | whileFalse _ _ _ hb' => rfl
815removed | whileTrue _ _ _ _ _ hb' hc' hl' => simp_all
816removed | whileTrue st st' st'' b c hb hc hloop ih1 ih2 =>
817removed cases e2 with
818removed | whileFalse _ _ _ hb' => simp_all
819removed | whileTrue _ st2' _ _ _ hb' hc' hl' =>
820removed have hst : st' = st2' := ih1 _ hc'
821removed subst hst
822removed exact ih2 _ hl'
823removed

841removedtheorem plus2_spec (st : State) (n : Nat) (st' : State)
842removed (hx : st[X] = n) (heval : st =[ plus2 ]=> st') :
843removed st'[X] = n + 2 := by

845removed -- `plus2` is an assignment, `st'` must be `st` extended at `X`.

847removed cases heval with
848removed | asgn _ _ m _ h =>
849removed simp only [Aexp.eval_plus, Aexp.eval_id, Aexp.eval_num] at h
850removed rw [TotalMap.update_eq]
851removed lia

11removed-- Copied from `SubVerso.Compat` to avoid making generated projects depend on verso.
12removed-- We want to have info state and messages available right after the elaboration,
13removed-- so we need to disable `Elab.async` which would let diagnostics produced asynchronously
14removed-- through spanshot tasks.
15removedprivate def commandWithoutAsync (act : CommandElabM Unit) : CommandElabM Unit := do
16removed match (← get).scopes with
17removed | [] => act
18removed | h :: t =>
19removed let mut orig : Option Bool := none
20removed try
21removed orig := h.opts.get? `Elab.async
22removed modify fun s => { s with scopes := { h with opts := h.opts.setBool `Elab.async false } :: t }
23removed act
24removed finally
25removed if let h :: t := (← get).scopes then
26removed let opts := orig.map (h.opts.setBool `Elab.async) |>.getD (h.opts.erase `Elab.async)
27removed modify fun s => { s with scopes := { h with opts := opts } :: t }
28removed

30removed let savedState ← get
31removed try
32removed m
33removed finally
34removed let state ← get
35removed set { savedState with
36removed -- Preserve the info tree
37removed infoState := state.infoState
38removed messages := if keepMsgs then state.messages else savedState.messages }

42removed/-! # Block Commands Parser
43removed Parse an indented command block. Commands are separated by new lines.
44removed Since we want to capture parsing errors in `sf_expect_failure`,
45removed we can't use Lean command parser directly in our command's syntax,
46removed because any parsing error occurred would fail `sf_expect_failure` itself.
47removed One possible solution is to first parse the whole indented body as raw syntax,
48removed and then run Lean's command parser followed by command elaboration.
49removed-/
50removed
51removedopen Parser
52removed
53removedprivate def rawLineEndFn : ParserFn :=
54removed eoiFn <|> satisfyFn (· == '\n') "line break"
55removed
56removed/-- Consumes everything until the next newline and then consumes the newline itself. -/
57removedprivate def rawLineFn : ParserFn :=
58removed takeUntilFn (· == '\n') >> rawLineEndFn
59removed
60removed/- For each line after the first body line, consumes leading whitespaces.
61removed If it's blank, consumes the newline; otherwise consumes the line
62removed requiring the indentation.
63removed-/
64removedprivate def rawIndentedLineFn : ParserFn := atomicFn <|
65removed takeWhileFn (· == ' ') >>
66removed (satisfyFn (· == '\n') "line break" <|>
67removed (checkColGeFn "indented command sequence" >> rawLineFn))
68removed
69removedprivate def rawCommandBlockFn : ParserFn :=
70removed rawFn (rawLineFn >> manyFn rawIndentedLineFn) (trailingWs := true)
71removed
72removedprivate def rawCommandBlock : Parser := { fn := rawCommandBlockFn }
73removed
74removed@[combinator_parenthesizer rawCommandBlock]
75removedprivate def rawCommandBlock.parenthesizer := PrettyPrinter.Parenthesizer.visitToken
76removed
77removed@[combinator_formatter rawCommandBlock]
78removedprivate def rawCommandBlock.formatter := PrettyPrinter.Formatter.visitAtom Name.anonymous
79removed
80removedprivate partial def runRawCmdsAux
81removed (ictx : InputContext) (pstate : ModuleParserState) : CommandElabM Unit := do
82removed let state ← get
83removed let scope := state.scopes.head!
84removed let pctx := {
85removed env := state.env
86removed options := scope.opts
87removed currNamespace := scope.currNamespace
88removed openDecls := scope.openDecls : ParserModuleContext
89removed }
90removed let (cmd, pstate, messages) := parseCommand ictx pctx pstate state.messages
91removed modify fun state => { state with messages }
92removed unless cmd.isOfKind ``Command.eoi do
93removed elabCommand cmd
94removed runLinters cmd
95removed unless isTerminalCommand cmd do
96removed runRawCmdsAux ictx pstate
97removed
98removed/- Recovers the source info and elaborates the commands -/
99removedprivate def runRawCmds (body : Syntax) : CommandElabM Unit := do
100removed let some source := body.getSubstring? (withLeading := false) (withTrailing := false)
101removed | throwErrorAt body "command sequence has no source range"
102removed let fileName ← getFileName
103removed let fileMap ← getFileMap
104removed -- Recall that `rawIndentedLineFn` may consume whitespaces after the newline.
105removed -- Here we move the ending back to the last non-whitespace character to produce
106removed -- correctly positioned diagnostics.
107removed let stopPos := source.trimRight.stopPos
108removed if h : stopPos ≤ fileMap.source.rawEndPos then
109removed let ictx := InputContext.mk fileMap.source fileName
110removed (fileMap := fileMap) (endPos := stopPos) (endPos_valid := h)
111removed runRawCmdsAux ictx { pos := source.startPos, recovering := false, hasLeading := false }
112removed else
113removed throwErrorAt body "invalid command-sequence source range"
114removed
115removedend IndentedCommands
116removed
117removedend
118removed
119removedpublic meta section
120removed
121removedopen Parser IndentedCommands
122removed
123removed/--
124removedElaborates the enclosed commands and reports their diagnostics,
125removedbut discards their effects afterwards.
126removed
127removedExample:
128removed```lean
129removedsf_experiment
130removed def hidden : Nat := 1
131removed #check hidden
132removed-- `hidden` is not available here.
133removed```
134removed-/
135removeddef experimentTk := leading_parser
136removed "sf_experiment"
137removed
138removed@[command_parser] def experimentCmd := leading_parser
139removed experimentTk >> checkLinebreakBefore "indented command sequence" >>
140removed checkColGt "indented command sequence" >> withPosition rawCommandBlock
141removed
142removed/--
143removedSucceeds only if the enclosed commands fail.
144removedDiagnostics from the expected failure are suppressed.
145removed
146removedExample:
147removed```lean
148removedsf_expect_failure
149removed example : 1 = 2 := rfl
150removed```
151removed-/
152removeddef expectFailureTk := leading_parser
153removed "sf_expect_failure"
154removed
155removed/-
156removed Like `sf_expect_failure` but reports the diagnostics.
157removed-/
158removeddef expectFailureInfoTk := leading_parser
159removed "sf_expect_failure?"
160removed
161removed@[command_parser] def expectFailureCmd := leading_parser
162removed expectFailureTk >> checkLinebreakBefore "indented command sequence" >>
163removed checkColGt "indented command sequence" >> withPosition rawCommandBlock
164removed
165removed@[command_parser] def expectFailureInfoCmd := leading_parser
166removed expectFailureInfoTk >> checkLinebreakBefore "indented command sequence" >>
167removed checkColGt "indented command sequence" >> withPosition rawCommandBlock
168removed
169removed@[command_elab experimentCmd]
170removeddef elabExperimentCmd : CommandElab := fun stx => do
171removed let body := stx.getArgs.back!
172removed commandWithoutAsync <| withRestoringState true do
173removed runRawCmds body
174removed
175removed@[command_elab expectFailureCmd, command_elab expectFailureInfoCmd]
176removeddef elabExpectFailureCmd : CommandElab := fun stx => do
177removed let keepMsgs := stx.isOfKind ``expectFailureInfoCmd
178removed unless keepMsgs || stx.isOfKind ``expectFailureCmd do
179removed throwUnsupportedSyntax
180removed let tk := stx[0]
181removed let body := stx.getArgs.back!
182removed commandWithoutAsync <| withRestoringState keepMsgs do
183removed withRef tk <| failIfSucceeds <| runRawCmds body
184removed
185removedend
186removed

3removed-- # Slang: Arithmetic and Boolean Expressions
4removed
5removed-- Note to developers (Benjamin Pierce @bcpierce00):
6removed-- We need to figure out our approach to text width,
7removed-- especially for proofs. Quite a few proofs here don't
8removed-- render into the chosen page width, and for terse mode it
9removed-- will be worse.
10removed
11removed-- ## Arithmetic and Boolean Expressions
12removed
13removed-- ### Syntax
14removed
15removednamespace Slang
16removed
17removed-- Abstract syntax trees for arithmetic and boolean
18removed-- expressions:
19removed
20removedinductive Aexp where
21removed | num (n : Nat)
22removed | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
23removed | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
24removed | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp)
25removed
26removedinductive Bexp where
27removed | bool (b : Bool)
28removed | eq (a1 a2 : Aexp)
29removed | neq (a1 a2 : Aexp)
30removed | le (a1 a2 : Aexp)
31removed | gt (a1 a2 : Aexp)
32removed | not (b : Bexp)
33removed | and (b1 b2 : Bexp)
34removed
35removed-- ### Evaluation
36removed
37removed-- *Evaluating* an arithmetic expression produces a number.
38removed
39removeddef Aexp.eval (a : Aexp) : Nat :=
40removed match a with
41removed | num n => n
42removed | plus a1 a2 => a1.eval + a2.eval
43removed | minus a1 a2 => a1.eval - a2.eval
44removed | mult a1 a2 => a1.eval * a2.eval
45removed
46removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_num (n : Nat) : (num n).eval = n := rfl
47removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_plus (a1 a2 : Aexp) : (plus a1 a2).eval = a1.eval + a2.eval := rfl
48removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_minus (a1 a2 : Aexp) : (minus a1 a2).eval = a1.eval - a2.eval := rfl
49removed@[simp] theorem Aexp.eval_mult (a1 a2 : Aexp) : (mult a1 a2).eval = a1.eval * a2.eval := rfl
50removed
51removedexample : Aexp.eval (.plus (.num 2) (.num 2)) = 4 := by simp
52removed
53removed-- Similarly, evaluating a boolean expression yields a boolean,
54removed-- and we give it the same treatment.
55removed
56removeddef Bexp.eval (b : Bexp) : Bool :=
57removed match b with
58removed | bool b => b
59removed | eq a1 a2 => a1.eval == a2.eval
60removed | neq a1 a2 => a1.eval != a2.eval
61removed | le a1 a2 => a1.eval ≤ a2.eval
62removed | gt a1 a2 => a1.eval > a2.eval
63removed | not b1 => !eval b1
64removed | and b1 b2 => eval b1 && eval b2
65removed
66removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_bool (b : Bool) : (bool b).eval = b := rfl
67removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_eq (a1 a2 : Aexp) : (eq a1 a2).eval = (a1.eval == a2.eval) := rfl
68removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_neq (a1 a2 : Aexp) : (neq a1 a2).eval = (a1.eval != a2.eval) := rfl
69removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_le (a1 a2 : Aexp) : (le a1 a2).eval = (a1.eval ≤ a2.eval : Bool) := rfl
70removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_gt (a1 a2 : Aexp) : (gt a1 a2).eval = (a1.eval > a2.eval : Bool) := rfl
71removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_not (b : Bexp) : (not b).eval = !b.eval := rfl
72removed@[simp] theorem Bexp.eval_and (b1 b2 : Bexp) : (and b1 b2).eval = (b1.eval && b2.eval) := rfl
73removed
74removed-- It's worth noting that `≤` and `>` are `Prop`-valued, i.e.
75removed-- `a1.eval st ≤ a2.eval st` is a proposition, but `Bexp.eval`
76removed-- returns a `Bool` so Lean implicitly inserts a `decide`
77removed-- coercion. You can observe the call to `decide` by hovering
78removed-- over `Bexp.eval_le` and `Bexp.eval_gt`.
79removed
80removed-- _Quiz:_
81removed
82removed-- What does the following expression evaluate to?
83removed
84removed-- Aexp.eval (.plus (.num 3) (.minus (.num 4) (.num 1)))
85removed
86removed-- (A) true (B) false (C) 0 (D) 3 (E) 6
87removed
88removed-- ### Optimization
89removed
90removeddef Aexp.optimize0plus (a : Aexp) : Aexp :=
91removed match a with
92removed | num n => num n
93removed | plus (num 0) e2 => optimize0plus e2
94removed | plus e1 e2 => plus (optimize0plus e1) (optimize0plus e2)
95removed | minus e1 e2 => minus (optimize0plus e1) (optimize0plus e2)
96removed | mult e1 e2 => mult (optimize0plus e1) (optimize0plus e2)
97removed
98removedexample :
99removed Aexp.optimize0plus (.plus (.num 2)
100removed (.plus (.num 0)
101removed (.plus (.num 0) (.num 1))))
102removed = .plus (.num 2) (.num 1) := by rfl
103removed
104removedtheorem optimize0plus_sound (a : Aexp) :
105removed a.optimize0plus.eval = a.eval := by
106removed induction a with
107removed | num n => rfl
108removed | plus a1 a2 ih1 ih2 =>
109removed cases a1 with
110removed | num n =>
111removed cases n with
112removed | zero =>
113removed simp only [Aexp.optimize0plus, Aexp.eval_plus, Aexp.eval_num, Nat.zero_add]
114removed exact ih2
115removed | succ n =>
116removed simp only [Aexp.optimize0plus, Aexp.eval_plus, Aexp.eval_num]
117removed rw [ih2]
118removed | plus b1 b2 =>
119removed simp only [Aexp.optimize0plus, Aexp.eval_plus] at ih1 ⊢
120removed rw [ih1, ih2]
121removed | minus b1 b2 =>
122removed simp only [Aexp.optimize0plus, Aexp.eval_plus] at ih1 ⊢
123removed rw [ih1, ih2]
124removed | mult b1 b2 =>
125removed simp only [Aexp.optimize0plus, Aexp.eval_plus] at ih1 ⊢
126removed rw [ih1, ih2]
127removed | minus a1 a2 ih1 ih2 =>
128removed simp only [Aexp.optimize0plus, Aexp.eval_minus]
129removed rw [ih1, ih2]
130removed | mult a1 a2 ih1 ih2 =>
131removed simp only [Aexp.optimize0plus, Aexp.eval_mult]
132removed rw [ih1, ih2]
133removed
134removedtheorem optimize0plus_sound' (a : Aexp) :
135removed a.optimize0plus.eval = a.eval := by
136removed fun_induction Aexp.optimize0plus a <;> simp_all
137removed
138removed-- ### Exercise (3 stars): optimize0plusB_sound ⭐⭐⭐
139removed
140removed-- Since the `Aexp.optimize0plus` transformation doesn't change
141removed-- the value of an `Aexp`, we should be able to apply it to all
142removed-- the `Aexp`s that appear in a `Bexp` without changing the
143removed-- `Bexp`'s value. Write a function that performs this
144removed-- transformation on `Bexp`s and prove it sound. Use the
145removed-- combinators we've just seen to make the proof as short and
146removed-- elegant as possible.
147removed
148removeddef Bexp.optimize0plusB (b : Bexp) : Bexp := sorry
149removed
150removedexample :
151removed Bexp.optimize0plusB
152removed (.not (.gt (.plus (.num 0) (.num 4)) (.num 8)))
153removed = (.not (.gt (.num 4) (.num 8))) := sorry
154removed
155removedexample :
156removed Bexp.optimize0plusB
157removed (.and (.le (.plus (.num 0) (.num 4)) (.num 5)) (.bool true))
158removed = (.and (.le (.num 4) (.num 5)) (.bool true)) := sorry
159removed
160removedtheorem optimize0plusB_sound (b : Bexp) :
161removed b.optimize0plusB.eval = b.eval := by
162removed sorry

164removed-- ### Exercise (4 stars): optimize ⭐⭐⭐⭐
165removed
166removed-- The optimization implemented by our `Aexp.optimize0plus` is
167removed-- only one of many possible optimizations on arithmetic and
168removed-- boolean expressions. Write a more sophisticated optimizer
169removed-- and prove it correct. (You will probably find it easiest to
170removed-- start small -- add just a single, simple optimization and
171removed-- its correctness proof -- and build up incrementally to
172removed-- something more interesting.)

174removed-- ## Evaluation as a Relation
175removed
176removedinductive Aexp.EvalR : Aexp → Nat → Prop where
177removed | num (n : Nat) : EvalR (.num n) n
178removed | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
179removed EvalR (.plus a1 a2) (n1 + n2)
180removed | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
181removed EvalR (.minus a1 a2) (n1 - n2)
182removed | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
183removed EvalR (.mult a1 a2) (n1 * n2)
184removed
185removed-- One comment on the style of this definition. We could
186removed-- instead have presented this relation with **positional**
187removed-- hypotheses -- no names for the premises.
188removed
189removednamespace ArithUnnamed
190removed
191removedinductive Aexp.EvalR : Aexp → Nat → Prop where
192removed | num (n : Nat) : EvalR (.num n) n
193removed | plus (e1 e2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) : EvalR e1 n1 → EvalR e2 n2 → EvalR (.plus e1 e2) (n1 + n2)
194removed | minus (e1 e2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) : EvalR e1 n1 → EvalR e2 n2 → EvalR (.minus e1 e2) (n1 - n2)
195removed | mult (e1 e2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) : EvalR e1 n1 → EvalR e2 n2 → EvalR (.mult e1 e2) (n1 * n2)
196removed
197removedend ArithUnnamed
198removed
199removed-- It will be convenient to have an infix notation for
200removed-- `Aexp.EvalR`. We'll write `e ⇓ n` to mean that arithmetic
201removed-- expression `e` evaluates to value `n`.
202removed
203removedscoped notation:55 e:56 " ⇓ " n:56 => Aexp.EvalR e n

237removed-- ### Exercise (1 star): beval_rules ⭐

239removed-- Here, again, is the definition of the `Bexp.eval` function:

254removed-- ### Equivalence of the Definitions
255removed
256removed-- It is straightforward to prove that the relational and
257removed-- functional definitions of evaluation agree.
258removed
259removedtheorem Aexp.evalR_iff_eval (a : Aexp) (n : Nat) :
260removed a ⇓ n ↔ a.eval = n := by
261removed constructor
262removed · intro h
263removed induction h with
264removed | num n => rfl
265removed | plus a1 a2 n1 n2 h1 h2 ih1 ih2 => simp only [Aexp.eval_plus]; rw [ih1, ih2]
266removed | minus a1 a2 n1 n2 h1 h2 ih1 ih2 => simp only [Aexp.eval_minus]; rw [ih1, ih2]
267removed | mult a1 a2 n1 n2 h1 h2 ih1 ih2 => simp only [Aexp.eval_mult]; rw [ih1, ih2]
268removed · intro h
269removed subst h
270removed induction a with
271removed | num n => exact .num n
272removed | plus a1 a2 ih1 ih2 => exact .plus a1 a2 _ _ ih1 ih2
273removed | minus a1 a2 ih1 ih2 => exact .minus a1 a2 _ _ ih1 ih2
274removed | mult a1 a2 ih1 ih2 => exact .mult a1 a2 _ _ ih1 ih2
275removed
276removed-- We can make the proof quite a bit shorter using more
277removed-- automation like we did in the previous section.
278removed
279removed-- Note to developers (Michael Hicks @mwhicks1, before next release):
280removed-- the `workinclass!` marker should signal this live
281removed-- in-class exercise. But it is not rendering properly on
282removed-- the HTML. In fact it replaces `workinclass!` with the
283removed-- `all_goals` tactic, which we don't need.
284removed
285removedtheorem Aexp.evalR_iff_eval' (a : Aexp) (n : Nat) :
286removed a ⇓ n ↔ a.eval = n := by
287removed sorry

311removed-- ### Computational vs. Relational Definitions
312removed
313removed-- Sometimes relational definitions are the only reasonable
314removed-- option...
315removed
316removednamespace Slang.AevalRDivision
317removed
318removed-- For example, suppose that we wanted to extend the arithmetic
319removed-- operations with division:
320removed
321removedinductive Aexp where
322removed | num (n : Nat)
323removed | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
324removed | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
325removed | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp)
326removed | div (a1 a2 : Aexp) -- NEW
327removed
328removed-- Extending the definition of `Aexp.eval` to handle this new
329removed-- operation would not be straightforward due to division being
330removed-- a *partial* operation; i.e., what should we return as the
331removed-- result of `.div (.num 5) (.num 0)`? By contrast, partiality
332removed-- is no problem for the relational version of the definition.
333removed
334removed-- What should `Aexp.eval` return for
335removed-- `.div (.num 1) (.num 0)`??
336removed
337removedinductive Aexp.EvalR : Aexp → Nat → Prop where
338removed | num (n : Nat) : EvalR (.num n) n
339removed | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
340removed EvalR (.plus a1 a2) (n1 + n2)
341removed | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
342removed EvalR (.minus a1 a2) (n1 - n2)
343removed | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
344removed EvalR (.mult a1 a2) (n1 * n2)
345removed | div (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 n3 : Nat) -- NEW
346removed (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) (hpos : n2 > 0) (hdiv : n2 * n3 = n1) :
347removed EvalR (.div a1 a2) n3
348removed
349removed-- Notice that there are some inputs (those with a divisor of
350removed-- 0) for which this relation does not specify an output.
351removed
352removedend Slang.AevalRDivision
353removed
354removednamespace Slang.AevalRExtended
355removed
356removed-- Another example: a *nondeterministic* number generator:
357removed
358removed-- As another example, suppose that we want to extend the
359removed-- arithmetic operations by a nondeterministic number generator
360removed-- `any` that, when evaluated, may yield any number. (This is
361removed-- not the same as making a *probabilistic* choice among all
362removed-- numbers -- we only say which results are *possible*.)
363removed
364removedinductive Aexp where
365removed | any -- NEW
366removed | num (n : Nat)
367removed | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
368removed | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp)
369removed | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp)
370removed
371removed-- Again, extending `Aexp.eval` would be tricky, since
372removed-- evaluation is now *not* a deterministic function from
373removed-- expressions to numbers; but extending the relation is no
374removed-- problem.
375removed
376removed-- What should `Aexp.eval` do with nondeterminism??
377removed
378removedinductive Aexp.EvalR : Aexp → Nat → Prop where
379removed | any (n : Nat) : EvalR .any n -- NEW
380removed | num (n : Nat) : EvalR (.num n) n
381removed | plus (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
382removed EvalR (.plus a1 a2) (n1 + n2)
383removed | minus (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
384removed EvalR (.minus a1 a2) (n1 - n2)
385removed | mult (a1 a2 : Aexp) (n1 n2 : Nat) (h1 : EvalR a1 n1) (h2 : EvalR a2 n2) :
386removed EvalR (.mult a1 a2) (n1 * n2)
387removed
388removedend Slang.AevalRExtended
389removed

391removed-- The following text seems not quite right to me. First,
392removed-- you can use options for partial functions, and that's

394removed-- related, monadic functions need not even be terminating

396removed-- a `partial_fixpoint`. Maybe we don't want to get into
397removed-- the second thing here, but failing to mention options

402removed-- Agreed.
